Ganesh Singh
 Versus
 Saligram Gadari And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Mohammad Afjal Sheikh - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Amrit Kaur Ruprah - Advocate for the respondent No.3.
 None for the respondent No.1 and 2.
 Order

This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 against the award dated 31.07.2023 passed in MACC.No.18/2020 by the Member 10th Additional M.A.C.T., Jabalpur District- Jabalpur, seeking enhancement of compensation.
2 . Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to the impugned award as well as Ex. P/12 to P/17, submits that tribunal has not granted amount of medical bills (Ex. P/12 to P/17).
It is also urged that appellant suffered fracture of tibia fibula and only Rs.6,000/- has been awarded for pain and suffering.
Further, for loss of income only Rs.6,500/- has been awarded.
On above grounds, it is urged that amount awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
3 . Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 submits that findings recorded by the tribunal are just and proper and no interference is required in the same.
Hence appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text: So far as medical expenses are concerned, it is correct that tribunal has not awarded amount of medical bills (Ex. P/12 to P/17) b ut reason for the same has been discussed in para 16 of impugned award.
This Court has examined documents filed by the appellant (Ex. P/12 to P/17) as well as findings recorded by the tribunal in para 16 of impugned award.
Perusal of the impugned award reveals that tribunal has not awarded amount of medical bills (Ex. P/13 to P/17) on the ground that they do not match with facts as mentioned in the discharge summary.

Perusal of Ex. P/12 and P/13 reveals that during admission in Shri Shubham Hospital and Research Centre, no operation was performed and it is also not mentioned in the discharge summary that when appellant was admitted in the hospital, he was bleeding.
Hence, in view of above, there appears to be no requirement of blood transfusion.

But in bill Ex.
P/13, an amount of Rs. 5,000/- is mentioned under the head of blood transfusion etc.

6. In view of above, in this court's opinion, finding recorded by the tribunal in para 16 to the effect that bills Ex. P/13 to P/17 do not match with the facts mentioned in discharge summary appears to be correct and no interference is required in the same.
Hence, appellant is not entitled to receive amount of bills (Ex. P/12 to P/17).
7. So far as enhancement under other head is concerned, in the instant case, appellant has suffered fracture of tibia fibula.
Therefore, it may be presumed that appellant was not able to work for at least 3 months.
Therefore, appellant is entitled to receive Rs.19,500/- for loss of income during treatment period.
Further, in view of fracture suffered by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:736 3 MA-13-2024 appellant, appellant is also entitled to receive Rs.25,000/- for pain and suffering.
In the instant case, tribunal has awarded Rs. 6,000/- for pain and suffering and Rs. 6,500/- for loss of income during treatment period.
8. Hence, in view of above appellant is entitled to receive Rs. 32,000/- as enhanced amount over and above the amount awarded by the tribunal.
9. Enhanced amount Rs. 32,000/- shall carry interest at the rate determined by the Tribunal.
Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
10. With the aforesaid directions, this appeal is partly allowed and disposed off.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE L.R.
